entry.title: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory Researchers Confirm Proof of Altermagnetism
entry.content:
Links: sciencedaily.com | www6.slac.stanford.edu | hacker news

Researchers at the U.S. Department of Energy's SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory have provided conclusive experimental evidence confirming altermagnetism, a third major phase of magnetism. Using circularly polarized X-rays at the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility, the team detected a distinct chiral signature in manganese telluride, a material previously classified solely as a conventional antiferromagnet.

While traditional ferromagnets produce external magnetic fields and antiferromagnets feature opposing spins that completely cancel out magnetization, altermagnets combine zero net magnetization with the ability to generate spin-polarized currents. This unique configuration offers stability against external magnetic interference alongside efficient spin-based information transport, presenting potential applications for advanced computer memory, quantum devices, and energy-efficient data centers.

Researchers analyzing data from the STAR experiment at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) have found strong evidence of quark-gluon plasma—a primordial state of matter from the early universe—produced by colliding oxygen nuclei. By measuring high-energy particle streams, the team observed a 20 percent suppression of particles, known as jet quenching, indicating that the dense plasma forms even in smaller and lower-energy collision systems than previously demonstrated.

While quark-gluon plasma has traditionally been studied using massive gold nuclei or at higher energies at CERN's Large Hadron Collider, the new RHIC findings establish a lower boundary for the conditions required to create this early-universe matter. The measurements, conducted using oxygen data collected before RHIC concluded operations in early 2026, help physicists better understand the minimal thresholds necessary for primordial matter to emerge.

entry.title: Medicare Reimbursement for Coronary Artery Calcium Scans
entry.content:
Links: medpagetoday.com | hacker news

Medicare provides significantly higher reimbursement for treating heart attacks than for preventative measures like coronary artery calcium scans. Medical guidelines have recently updated to support the use of calcium scans to identify cardiovascular risk prior to a cardiac event.

The current funding disparity highlights a gap between acute treatment costs and preventative diagnostic tools. Increasing coverage for these scans is proposed as a method to reduce the long-term financial burden of heart disease on the healthcare system.

entry.title: Researchers Publish Study on 25,000 Psychedelic Support Line Interactions
entry.content:
Links: 404media.co | science.org

Researchers have published a study in Science Advances analyzing the Fireside Database, a collection of 25,419 anonymized peer-support interactions from the Fireside Project’s Psychedelic Support Line between April 2021 and February 2026. This dataset represents the largest compilation of real-world psychedelic experiences outside of clinical environments, encompassing substances such as psilocybin, LSD, cannabis, ketamine, and MDMA.

The study found high rates of distress across substances, with cannabis users reporting the highest rate of bad experiences at 47.2 percent, closely followed by traditional psychedelics ranging from 40 to 42 percent. Additionally, the analysis documented 43 instances of facilitator abuse in unregulated or ceremonial settings and highlighted that a caller's satisfaction was heavily dependent on perceiving genuine empathy from hotline volunteers.
